``` r
#' Merge matrices from dv8-dsm file
#'
#' @param dv8_dsm_path_list list of paths to multiple dv8-dsm files
#' @param merged_dv8_dsm_path path to save merged dv8-dsm file
#' @export
dv8_hsdsmb_sdsmb_to_hsdsmb <- function(dv8_dsm_path_list, merged_dv8_dsm_path){
  # Expand paths (e.g. "~/Desktop" => "/Users/someuser/Desktop")
  merged_dv8_dsm_path <- path.expand(merged_dv8_dsm_path)

    system2('dv8-console', args=c('core:merge-matrix', '-outputFile', merged_dv8_dsm_path, path1, path2), stdout=FALSE, stderr=FALSE)

        # Run system2 command

      }
    }
  }
}

```

Hi Carlos,
I've created the parse_dv8_clusters() function. I utilized the example table you gave on the main DV8 issue (https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/issues/165#issuecomment-1477482636) to help me understand what I needed to do and how to format the table.

## Output

The table is composed of three columns: layer, module, and file. I used the DV8 user guide https://archdia.com/pages/dv8-user-guide to learn more about this clustering hierarchy.

Each row shows the current layer, the current module, and the current file. From what I observed, layers can have multiple modules, and modules can have multiple files.

## My Process
I went through the DV8 diagram process to get the clustering file to pass to the core::export-cluster command (which I made the wrapper dv8_clsxb_to_clsxj() for) and acquire a json file. I analyzed the structure of the json and learned more about the layer, module, file composition. This helped me build the parse_dv8_clusters() function.

## How parse_dv8_clusters() works
The parse_dv8_clusters() itself takes in a single parameter, the path to the clustering.json output from the core::export-cluster command/dv8_clsxb_to_clsxj(). Then, it iterates through each of the layers, each of the modules, and finally to the file level to extract a row for the data table I create at the end. Each row contains the layer number, module number, and the current file the loop is looking at in the current module. Each row is added to a list. This list of lists gets converted into a datatable at the end.

## Preview of table output (called project_hier)
Here is what the data table looks like. I have called it project-hier since the input to the function (following the diagram you provided for DV8) is called project-hier.json:

## parse_dv8_clusters() function
Here is what my parse_dv8_clusters() function looks like. I've explicitly shown the package names and have added comments to try and clarify each line of code. How does this look?

```r
#' Parse project-hier.json from DV8
#'
#' @param clustering_path path to project-hier.json (obtained from dv8_clsxb_to_clsxj)
#' @export
#' @family parsers
parse_dv8_clusters <- function(clustering_path){
  # Read in the clustering file
  dv8_clusters_json <- jsonlite::read_json(clustering_path)
  
  # Get number of cluster layers in the json
  num_layers <- length(dv8_clusters_json$structure)
  
  # The structure field holds the relevant data
  structure <- dv8_clusters_json[["structure"]]
  
  # Will hold each row (a list of the current layer, module, and file) for the data table
  cluster_list <- list()
  
  # Iterate through each cluster
  for (i in 1: num_layers) {
    # Get the layer number (L0, L1, L2, ...)
    layer_i <- structure[[i]]$name
    
    # Get the number of modules for the current layer
    num_modules <- length(structure[[i]]$nested)
    
    # Iterate through each module
    for (j in 1: num_modules) {
      # Get the module number (M0, M1, M2, ...)
      LM_name <- stringr::str_split(structure[[i]]$nested[[j]]$name, "/")
      module_j <- LM_name[[1]][2]
      
      # Get number of files for the layer/module pair
      num_files_per_LM <- length(structure[[i]]$nested[[j]]$nested)
      
        # Iterate through each file
        for (k in 1: num_files_per_LM) {
          # Get the file name
          filename_k <- structure[[i]]$nested[[j]]$nested[[k]]$name
          
          # Represents a row in the table with the layer #, module #, and filename
          row_ijk <- list(layer_i, module_j, filename_k)
          
          # Append current row (made up of the layer number, module number, & filename) to a list
          cluster_list <- append(cluster_list, list(row_ijk))
        }
    }
  }
  
  # Create table from list of layer,module,file rows
  cluster_parsed <- data.table::rbindlist(cluster_list)
  
  # Rename result columns
  cluster_parsed <- dplyr::rename(cluster_parsed, "layer" = "V1", "module" = "V2", "filename" = "V3")
  
  # Return parsed cluster data table
  return(cluster_parsed)
}
```

```r
# Example of calling function
project_hier <- parse_dv8_clusters("../../../Downloads/project-hier.json")
project_hier
```
